paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Knowing the right answer is not the same as loving the right way. Paul says "Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up." (1 Corinthians 8:1) The well-informed believers had the facts straight: there is but one God, the Father, and one Lord, Jesus Christ (1 Corinthians 8:6).

But facts alone can leave you full of hot air, and I would know, because I have been a puffed-up stamper before. Paul says food does not bring us closer to God (1 Corinthians 8:8), so the real question is what your freedom does to the people watching you. He warns, "Be careful, however, that your freedom does not become a stumbling block to the weak." (1 Corinthians 8:9) Someone with a weak conscience is a brother "for whom Christ died" (1 Corinthians 8:11), and that is why he matters more than winning the argument.

So ask yourself, baker: who is watching me, and what do they learn from what I do? Paul doesn't just hand out the rule, he lives it. He says he will never eat meat again if it causes his brother to stumble (1 Corinthians 8:13). Love gives up a little of what it's allowed to do so somebody else can stand tall, and that is how you build people up.
